purpose: Resolve every Black-Ink Bestiary page from one universal coloring-book contract plus reusable monster/environment catalogs and a small set of page-unique facts.

derived_fields.habitat: environment profile name unless page overrides it
derived_fields.identity_rules: monster accuracy_checks plus optional page identity_rules
derived_fields.composition: universal defaults.composition unless page overrides it
derived_fields.coloring_rules: universal defaults.coloring_rules merged with page overrides
derived_fields.must_avoid: global_must_avoid + monster must_avoid + environment must_avoid + page must_avoid

defaults.composition: Portrait coloring page; the monster, object-creature, or creature group is the visually dominant focal subject through framing, placement, silhouette clarity, and contrast while preserving canonical creature scale and proportions. Tiny and small creatures may occupy less page height and must remain visibly small relative to human-scale architecture, props, traps, furniture, and openings; never enlarge them into medium/large heroic bodies merely to dominate the page. Large creatures may fill more of the frame when their canonical size supports it. Keep the full or nearly full silhouette readable. The environment must remain unmistakable using two to four large supporting forms arranged around, behind, or beneath the subject. At least one environmental feature must participate in the story moment. Preserve broad colorable regions, clear silhouette separation, believable grounding, and generous white space.

global_must_avoid: decorative artwork border or inset frame
environment disconnected from the story moment
clutter that obscures monster, habitat, or story beat
accidental hovering or unsupported standing pose
tiny repeated texture that creates coloring homework
non-flying creature shown jumping, falling, dropping, or frozen in midair
chaotic action pose that makes anatomy difficult to read or color

page_uniqueness.rule: Pages may reuse a monster family or environment family, but should not reuse the same resolved combination of subject, place, landmark, framing, interaction, action, and physical state unless intentionally designed as a paired scene.

inheritance_rule: When a universal rule improves, every tome and future book inherits it automatically. Tome manifests store only page-specific recipes and exceptions.

environment_diversity.rule: A concrete environment profile may recur when appropriate, but must not dominate the book. For a 50-page tome, the same profile may appear at most four times. Consecutive use is capped at two pages. Unique landmarks, framing, interaction, and physicality are still required on every occurrence.

locomotion.rule: Coloring pages favor stable natural poses. Non-flying creatures must be visibly supported by the environment and may not be shown falling, jumping, leaping, dropping, hovering, or frozen in midair. Creatures with locomotion.can_fly=true may use controlled natural flight, but the pose must remain calm, readable, and easy to color.

product_scope.repeat_rule: Monster repeats are permitted only when the resolved page recipe is materially different in environment profile, landmark, framing, interaction, moment, and physical state.

approval_gate.rule: All gates must pass before Approve & Lock. Colorability is the first constraint: story may enrich a page but may never reduce coloring usability.

subject_scale_rules.tiny: Preserve unmistakably tiny creature scale. Use closer framing, grouping, or nearby scale references for visual importance; never give the creature adult-humanoid mass or heroic proportions.
subject_scale_rules.small: Preserve unmistakably small creature scale. Human-scale doors, corridors, furniture, traps, tools, and masonry should make the creature read small; use camera/framing for emphasis rather than enlarging its body.
subject_scale_rules.medium: Preserve normal medium creature scale and species-specific proportions; do not inflate the body into giant or bodybuilder mass unless canonical anatomy explicitly requires it.
subject_scale_rules.large: Preserve clearly large creature scale using architecture, terrain, furniture, or other scale references; size must come from canonical mass/proportions rather than heroic bodybuilding.
subject_scale_rules.huge: Preserve huge scale with strong environmental scale references and enough surrounding geometry to prove the size.
subject_scale_rules.gargantuan: Preserve gargantuan scale with unmistakable environmental comparison; avoid shrinking the creature into a normal room-sized subject.
subject_scale_rules.swarm: The swarm is visually dominant as a collective group, while each member retains its canonical individual scale. No oversized leader or mascot creature.
subject_scale_rules.default: Preserve the creature's canonical size and proportions. Achieve visual dominance through framing and placement, never by changing species scale.
